source.title: Stochastic resetting mitigates latent gradient bias of SGD from label noise
source.authors: Youngkyoung Bae; Yeongwoo Song; Hawoong Jeong

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses double descent briefly but does not test any of the listed double-descent versions or rely on them as a method or assumption.
record.gate_note: The paper mentions double descent when discussing checkpoint selection and as a limitation, but reports no test-error sweep over model size, epochs, or sample size. Figure 1(b) concerns accuracy on mislabeled training examples, not test error; it is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The paper mentions double descent only twice: when the minimum-validation-loss checkpoint is chosen (citing Nakkiran et al.) and as a limitation of its resetting method. It reports no test-error sweep over model size, epochs or sample size aimed at double descent. Its training curves under label noise show validation loss falling then rising, an early-stopping/memorization pattern. No second descent is examined, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially right. The authors conclude that resetting to the minimum-validation-loss checkpoint mitigates a latent gradient bias from label noise and improves test accuracy, with larger gains at smaller batch sizes and higher noise rates. They name double descent only as a case where the method may be less effective.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes stochastic resetting for SGD on noisy-label tasks; it does not reproduce the original double-descent method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that resetting benefits vary with checkpoint choice, batch size, noise rate, and which network section is reset; these are settings for its resetting method, not double-descent tests.

fits_no_version.finding: Under label noise, accuracy on the true labels of mislabeled training examples follows an inverted-U over training, while validation loss rises after an early minimum. Stochastic resetting to the minimum-validation checkpoint suppresses this.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under label noise, SGD-trained networks first learn clean patterns and then memorize corrupted labels. Resetting to an early-learning checkpoint mitigates this memorization.

record.problems: No direct evidence on any listed double-descent version. The adjacent training-curve evidence is figure-based and concerns mislabeled training examples rather than test error.

untested.parts: Validation-loss and test-accuracy curves over iterations are shown (Fig. 1b inset, Fig. 4a), but double descent is not examined. The authors note their method may fail if double descent occurs; they do not report whether it does.
No sample-size sweep. Sec. A.2 only argues theoretically that a small dataset adds gradient bias.
No capacity sweep across model classes.
Label-noise rate is varied, but only for resetting gains. Neither the peak's dependence on noise or regularization nor multiple peaks is studied.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from discusses to cites_only: double descent appears only as a citation and as a stated limitation, not as a subject of analysis. Tranche T6 is kept.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep or test-error curve.
No training-sample-size sweep near an interpolation threshold.
No capacity sweep across model classes.
No common effective-complexity measure or prediction of peak location.
The paper studies noisy labels and resetting, but does not test noise or regularization dependence of a double-descent peak, multiple peaks, or disappearance under optimal regularization.
No re-counting of complexity by effective parameters or comparison to an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: DNN
rows.operation_detail: Tracks the fraction of correctly predicted true labels among training examples with corrupted labels during SGD.
rows.measure: Fraction of correctly predicted true labels among examples with wrong labels
rows.note: The text describes this measure as having an inverted-U trajectory as the model memorizes corrupted labels. It is not test error.
rows.check: Measures accuracy on the true labels of mislabeled training examples (memorization), not test error. Linking to none is correct.

rows.subject: DNN
rows.operation_detail: Applies stochastic resetting during SGD and tracks the fraction of correctly predicted true labels among training examples with corrupted labels.
rows.measure: Fraction of correctly predicted true labels among examples with wrong labels
rows.baseline: SGD without resetting; numerical baseline not stated
rows.note: The figure shows a separate resetting curve, but the text does not quantify its value. This measure is not test error.
rows.check: This is the study's own method (resetting) compared with plain SGD on a memorization measure; it is not a double-descent measurement. Linking to none is correct.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
